## 1. The golden rules

1. **Never push to `main`.** `main` is production and is protected. Only the owner releases to it.
2. **Never commit straight to `dev`.** `dev` is the shared integration branch. Your work reaches `dev` only through a **pull request** that has been reviewed and has green CI.
3. **One issue = one branch = one pull request.** Branch name: `feature/<issue>-<short-name>`.
4. **Always start a branch from the latest `dev`.**
5. **Never commit secrets.** Keys live only in `.env.local`, which is git-ignored.
6. **Don't apply database migrations yourself.** Commit the SQL file; the owner applies it.
7. Run the checks (tests, type check, build) **before** you push for review.

## 2. Branches: what goes where

| Branch | What it is | Who pushes | Deploys to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | Production | Owner only (protected) | https://yulabs-crm-1122.netlify.app |
| `dev` | Integration of everyone's finished work | Merged PRs only | https://dev--yulabs-crm-1122.netlify.app |
| `feature/<issue>-<name>` | Your work on one issue | **You** | nothing (CI runs on the PR) |

```
[your laptop]  feature/5-api-keys
      |
      |  git push -u origin feature/5-api-keys
      v
[GitHub]       feature/5-api-keys
      |
      |  pull request (base: dev) -> CI green -> review -> squash-merge
      v
[GitHub]       dev    -> auto-deploys https://dev--yulabs-crm-1122.netlify.app
      |
      |  owner only: release PR dev -> main
      v
[GitHub]       main   -> auto-deploys https://yulabs-crm-1122.netlify.app
```

**Where you push:** `git push -u origin feature/<issue>-<name>`. That always goes to your own feature branch on `origin`. Then open a PR with **base = `dev`**.

## 3. One-time setup

### 3.1 Install the tools

| Tool | Version | Check |
|---|---|---|
| Git | 2.40+ | `git --version` |
| Node.js | **22** (same as CI) | `node -v` |
| npm | comes with Node | `npm -v` |
| GitHub CLI (optional, recommended) | latest | `gh --version` |
| VS Code (or Cursor) | latest | |
| cloudflared (only for webhook testing) | latest | `cloudflared --version` |

Windows: use **Git Bash** or PowerShell. All commands below work in both unless noted.

### 3.2 Tell Git who you are (once per computer)

```bash
git config --global user.name "Charan Varigonda"
git config --global user.email "<the email on your GitHub account>"
git config --global pull.rebase true
git config --global init.defaultBranch main
```

### 3.3 Sign in to GitHub

```bash
gh auth login          # choose GitHub.com → HTTPS → login with a web browser
gh auth status         # should say: Logged in to github.com account CHARANVARIGONDA
```

Without `gh`, Git asks for credentials on your first push. Use the browser sign-in window (Git Credential Manager) or a Personal Access Token, **not** your password.

### 3.4 Clone the repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/yulabs-in/CRM-Based-Voice-Agents.git
cd CRM-Based-Voice-Agents
git checkout dev
git pull
```

> Older clones may point at `yulabs-in/screenshot-exact-match`, the repository's old name. GitHub redirects it, but you can update it with `git remote set-url origin https://github.com/yulabs-in/CRM-Based-Voice-Agents.git`.

### 3.5 Install dependencies

```bash
npm ci                 # exact versions from package-lock.json (same as CI)
```

Use `npm ci`, not `npm install`, unless you are adding a package on purpose. If you do add a package (`npm install <pkg>`), commit both `package.json` **and** `package-lock.json`.

### 3.6 Environment variables

```bash
cp .env.example .env.local
```

`.env` (committed) holds the public Supabase values. `.env.local` (git-ignored) holds the server secrets. **Ask the team lead** for the values for `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `SARVAM_API_KEY` and `PUBLIC_APP_URL`. Never paste them into chat, issues, PRs, code or screenshots.

Check that Git ignores the file:

```bash
git check-ignore .env.local      # must print: .env.local
```

### 3.7 Run the app

```bash
npm run dev
```

Open the **Local** URL that Vite prints (for example `http://localhost:8080`). Sign up or sign in, and you should see the dashboard. Stop it with `Ctrl+C`.

### 3.8 Run the tests once, so you know the baseline

```bash
npx vitest run
npx tsc --noEmit       # 10 known errors exist today, so note the number you see
npm run build
```

## 4. Daily development loop

### 4.1 Start an issue

```bash
git checkout dev
git pull                                   # get everyone's latest merged work
git checkout -b feature/5-api-keys       # new branch from dev
```

On GitHub, comment on the issue: "Starting on this today. Branch `feature/5-api-keys`."

### 4.2 Work in small steps

```bash
npm run dev                  # keep it running; the page reloads on save
npx vitest                   # optional: tests in watch mode in a second terminal
```

### 4.3 See what changed

```bash
git status                   # which files changed
git diff                     # the exact lines
```

### 4.4 Commit

```bash
git add src/routes/_authenticated/_app/profile.tsx src/components/app/AppShell.tsx
git commit -m "Profile: upload and remove avatar"
```

- Add files **by name**. Avoid `git add .` unless you've checked `git status` and nothing unexpected (`.env.local`, `dist/`, `.netlify/`, screenshots) is listed.
- One idea per commit; present-tense message under ~70 characters; details in the body if needed.

### 4.5 Push your branch (do this often; it is your backup)

```bash
git push -u origin feature/5-api-keys    # first push: creates the branch on GitHub
git push                                   # later pushes
```

This pushes only to **your feature branch**. It never touches `dev` or `main`.

### 4.6 Stay up to date with `dev` (at least daily, and before opening a PR)

```bash
git fetch origin
git rebase origin/dev        # replay your commits on top of the latest dev
# if there are conflicts: fix the files, then
git add <fixed files>
git rebase --continue
# when the rebase is done, update your remote branch:
git push --force-with-lease
```

`--force-with-lease` is safe on **your own** feature branch, because it refuses to overwrite commits you haven't seen. **Never force-push `dev` or `main`.**

Prefer merging? `git merge origin/dev`, then a normal `git push`. Either is fine; just be consistent within a branch.

## 5. Testing: what to run, and when

### 5.1 Automated checks (every PR, CI runs the first and third too)

```bash
npx vitest run               # all unit tests
npx vitest run src/test/crm-outcome.test.ts    # one file
npx vitest -t "interested"   # tests whose name matches
npx tsc --noEmit             # type check: no NEW errors
npm run build                # production build must succeed
npm run lint                 # lint
```

### 5.2 Writing unit tests

- Put tests in `src/test/<thing>.test.ts`. Vitest with jsdom (see `src/test/crm-outcome.test.ts` for the house style).
- Test **pure functions** first: parsers, rule lookups, permission checks, mappers. Move logic out of components and server routes into small functions so you can test it.
- Freeze time when it matters: `vi.useFakeTimers(); vi.setSystemTime(new Date("2026-11-23T10:00:00+05:30"))`.
- Mock network and Sarvam: `vi.mock("@/lib/sarvam.server", () => ({ ... }))`. Tests must never call real Sarvam or send real messages.

Example:

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { classifyCallOutcome } from "@/lib/crm-outcome";

describe("classifyCallOutcome", () => {
  it("ignores calls that never connected", () => {
    expect(classifyCallOutcome({ status: "no_answer", answers: { disposition: "interested" } })).toBeNull();
  });

  it("qualifies an interested caller", () => {
    const r = classifyCallOutcome({ status: "completed", answers: { disposition: "interested" } });
    expect(r).toMatchObject({ leadStatus: "qualified", dealStage: "qualification" });
  });
});
```

### 5.3 Manual testing checklist

- [ ] The happy path works end to end.
- [ ] Error paths: empty input, bad input, network error. You see friendly messages, not a blank screen.
- [ ] Loading states show (throttle the network in DevTools → Network → "Slow 4G").
- [ ] Desktop width **and** 375 px (DevTools → device toolbar → iPhone SE).
- [ ] Keyboard only: Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Esc.
- [ ] Reload the page: state persisted where it should.
- [ ] **Security:** signed in as a second user in another workspace (use a private window), you cannot see or change the first user's data.
- [ ] Browser console has no new errors or warnings.

### 5.4 Testing webhooks and real calls locally

Sarvam can't reach `localhost`, so open a tunnel:

```bash
cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:<port>
# copy the https://xxxx.trycloudflare.com URL into PUBLIC_APP_URL in .env.local, then restart npm run dev
```

You can also simulate a webhook without placing a call:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:<port>/api/public/sarvam-call-webhook \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @test-payload.json
```

Keep sample payloads out of Git if they contain real data, and **only ever call your own number** with test calls.

### 5.5 Database changes

- Write the SQL in `db/migrations/NNNN_short_name.sql`. NNNN = the highest number on `origin/dev` + 1, checked when you open the PR (`git fetch && git ls-tree --name-only origin/dev db/migrations/ | tail -3`).
- Every table: `organization_id`, RLS on, policies scoped to the user's memberships. Additive changes only.
- Add the new types to `src/integrations/supabase/types.ts` (or ask the lead to regenerate it).
- **Do not run it against Supabase.** In the PR description, say "Migration `00NN_…` needs applying". The owner applies it before merging, while dev and production still share one database.

## 6. Open a pull request into `dev`

### 6.1 Final checks

```bash
git fetch origin && git rebase origin/dev
npx vitest run && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build
git status                   # nothing unexpected; no .env.local, dist/, .netlify/
git push --force-with-lease  # or plain git push if you didn't rebase
```

### 6.2 Create the PR

**With GitHub CLI:**

```bash
gh pr create --base dev --head feature/5-api-keys \
  --title "#5 <issue title>" \
  --body "Closes #5

## What changed
- …

## How I tested
- npx vitest run (all green), npm run build OK
- Manual: …

## Screenshots
(before / after, desktop + 375 px)

## Migration
None | 00NN_name.sql needs applying"
```

**On the website:** open the repo → the yellow banner "feature/… had recent pushes" → **Compare & pull request** → set **base: `dev`** ← compare: your branch → fill in the title and body as above → **Create pull request**.

> Check the base branch: it must say **`dev`**. If it says `main`, change it (Edit next to the title).

Assign yourself, link the issue (`Closes #N` does this), and ask the team lead for review. Open it as a **Draft PR** early if you want feedback before it's finished: `gh pr create --draft …`.

### 6.3 CI and review

- CI runs `npx vitest run` and `npm run build` on every push to the PR. Watch it with `gh pr checks --watch` or in the PR's **Checks** tab.
- If CI is red, open the failed job log, fix the problem locally, commit, and push. The PR updates by itself.
- Review comments: fix them in new commits on the same branch, push, and reply "Done" (or explain) on each comment. Resolve conversations once they're handled.

```bash
gh pr view --web             # open your PR in the browser
gh pr status                 # your PRs and their checks
```

### 6.4 Merge

When CI is green and the PR is approved, the reviewer (or you, if told to) **squash-merges** into `dev`. Delete the branch on GitHub when asked (there's a button).

## 7. After the merge: check the dev preview

1. The push to `dev` triggers **Deploy** (GitHub → Actions). Wait for it to finish (a few minutes).
2. Open https://dev--yulabs-crm-1122.netlify.app and test your feature there, just as you did locally.
3. Comment on the issue: "Merged in #<PR>, verified on the dev preview." The issue closes automatically from `Closes #N`.
4. If something is broken on the preview, open a new small fix branch from `dev` straight away (`feature/<issue>-fix-<what>`).

### 7.1 Clean up locally and start the next issue

```bash
git checkout dev
git pull
git branch -d feature/5-api-keys         # delete the local branch (safe: refuses if unmerged)
git fetch --prune                          # forget branches deleted on GitHub
git checkout -b feature/<next-issue>-<name>
```

After a squash merge, `git branch -d` may say "not fully merged". If the PR shows **Merged**, use `git branch -D …`.

## 8. Fixing common problems

**I committed on `dev` (or `main`) by mistake, and haven't pushed:**

```bash
git branch feature/<issue>-<name>      # keep your commits on a new branch
git reset --hard origin/dev            # put local dev back (on main: origin/main)
git checkout feature/<issue>-<name>
```

**I started coding before creating a branch (nothing committed yet):**

```bash
git checkout -b feature/<issue>-<name>  # your uncommitted changes come with you
```

**Rebase conflict:**

```bash
git status                     # files marked "both modified"
# open each file, keep the right parts, remove <<<<<<< ======= >>>>>>> markers
git add <file>
git rebase --continue
# give up and go back to how it was before:
git rebase --abort
```

For `package-lock.json` conflicts: take dev's version, then reinstall your package:

```bash
git checkout origin/dev -- package-lock.json   # start from dev's lock file
npm install                                     # re-adds your package on top
git add package-lock.json && git rebase --continue
```

**I need to switch tasks with unfinished work:**

```bash
git stash push -m "wip profile"     # put it aside
git checkout other-branch
git checkout -                      # come back
git stash pop
```

**Undo the last commit but keep the changes:** `git reset --soft HEAD~1`

**I committed a secret:** stop. Don't push. If you **already pushed**, tell the team lead **immediately** so the key can be rotated. Removing it from Git history isn't enough once it has been pushed.

**`npm ci` fails:** check `node -v` is 22. Delete `node_modules` and run `npm ci` again.

**Push rejected (`non-fast-forward`):** someone else, or you on another machine, pushed to your branch. Run `git pull --rebase` and then `git push`.

**`Permission denied` / 403 on push:** run `gh auth status`. Make sure you're pushing a `feature/...` branch (not `main`) and that you accepted the repository invitation.

## #5: API keys and a public REST API

**Assignee:** Charan Varigonda · **Branch:** `feature/5-api-keys` · **Depends on:** nothing (use #16's permission map once it lands) · **Blocks:** #6 MCP server, #7 docs

**Why:** customers want to connect their own systems (website forms, sheets, dashboards) to the CRM.

**Build:**
1. Migration `api_keys`: `id`, `organization_id`, `name`, `key_prefix` (first 8 chars, shown in the UI), `key_hash` (SHA-256 hex, **never store the raw key**), `scopes text[]`, `created_by`, `last_used_at`, `revoked_at`, `created_at`. RLS: only owners and admins of the org can select, insert or update.
2. Scopes: `contacts:read`, `contacts:write`, `leads:read`, `deals:read`, `calls:read`, `calls:write`.
3. Key format: `yk_live_` + 32 random bytes base62 or hex (`crypto.getRandomValues`). Show it **once** with a copy button. After that, only the prefix is visible.
4. Settings → **API & MCP** page: create (name + scope checkboxes), list (name, prefix, scopes, created by, last used), revoke (with a confirm dialog).
5. Shared server helper `src/lib/api-auth.server.ts`: `authenticateApiKey(request, requiredScope)` → reads `Authorization: Bearer yk_live_…` → SHA-256 → finds an un-revoked key → checks the scope → returns `{ organizationId, keyId }`, or throws a 401/403 JSON error. #6 reuses this.
6. Routes under `src/routes/api/v1/` (copy the structure of `src/routes/api/public/*.ts`):
   - `GET /api/v1/contacts` (search `?q=`), `POST /api/v1/contacts`, `GET /api/v1/contacts/:id`, `PATCH /api/v1/contacts/:id`
   - `GET /api/v1/leads`, `GET /api/v1/deals`
   - `GET /api/v1/calls`, `GET /api/v1/calls/:id` (status, duration, answers, summary, transcript)
   - `POST /api/v1/calls`: places an AI call by reusing the logic in `startSarvamCall`. Requires `calls:write` and `consent_confirmed: true`, and refuses do-not-contact numbers.
7. Every query uses the service client **and** `.eq('organization_id', orgId)`. That filter is what keeps orgs apart.
8. Errors are always `{ "error": { "code": "unauthorized" | "forbidden" | "not_found" | "invalid_request" | "rate_limited", "message": "…" } }`. Pagination is `?limit=` (default 50, max 200) plus `?cursor=` (the last `created_at`/`id`). Responses include `next_cursor`.
9. Rate limit: for example 60 requests per minute per key (an in-memory map is fine to start; note the limitation). Update `last_used_at` on every request, at most once a minute.

**Test:**
- Unit tests (`src/test/api-auth.test.ts`): hashing, a valid key, a revoked key → 401, a missing scope → 403.
- With the dev server running:
  ```bash
  curl -s http://localhost:<port>/api/v1/contacts -H "Authorization: Bearer yk_live_xxx"
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:<port>/api/v1/contacts -H "Authorization: Bearer yk_live_xxx" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"name":"Test User","phone":"+919999999999"}'
  ```
- Revoke the key and repeat: you get 401. Use a key without `contacts:write` for the POST: you get 403.
- **Cross-org test:** a key from org A asks for a contact id from org B and must get 404. Write this as a test.

**Done when:** a key created in the UI works with `curl`, a revoked key gets 401, a key without the scope gets 403, and a key from org A can never read org B's data.

## #14: Notifications for new interested leads and escalations

**Assignee:** Charan Varigonda · **Branch:** `feature/14-notifications` · **Depends on:** nothing

**Why:** the team should hear about hot leads and escalations straight away.

**Build:**
1. Migration `notifications` (`id`, `organization_id`, `user_id`, `type`, `title`, `body`, `link`, `priority`, `read_at`, `created_at`). RLS: users see only their own. Add the table to the `supabase_realtime` publication.
2. Create notifications from `crm-sync.server.ts` (via a small `notify()` helper): new interested lead, consultation booked, escalation (high priority), do-not-contact request. Decide who receives each: the deal owner, otherwise admins and managers.
3. `NotificationBell.tsx` in `AppShell.tsx`: unread count badge, dropdown list, mark read, mark all read, click → `link`. Live through Supabase Realtime (`postgres_changes` on `notifications` filtered by `user_id`).
4. Optional: a morning email digest (yesterday's interested leads and pending follow-ups).

**Test:**
- Unit test for "who gets notified" per event type.
- Open the app in two browser windows as two users, simulate an interested webhook, and check the right user's bell updates **without a reload**.
- User B must not be able to read user A's notifications (try it from the browser console).

**Done when:** finishing an interested test call shows a notification within seconds, without a reload.

## #11: Consultation booking with calendar invites

**Assignee:** Charan Varigonda · **Branch:** `feature/11-consultation-booking` · **Depends on:** nothing

**Why:** a consultation booked on a call should land on the team's calendar automatically.

**Build:**
1. Time parser `src/lib/parse-followup-time.ts`: turns "tomorrow 11 AM", "day after tomorrow morning", "Monday evening", "25th at 3" into a datetime in **Asia/Kolkata**, relative to the call end time. Define defaults: morning = 10:00, afternoon = 14:00, evening = 18:00. Return `null` when unsure, and never guess wildly.
2. When the agent returns `consultation_booked` (or `callback` with `follow_up_time`), create a `meetings` row (the table exists) linked to the contact and deal from `crm-sync.server.ts`. Show it on the Meetings page and the contact timeline.
3. Owner assignment: the deal owner, otherwise round-robin among users with a chosen role (setting).
4. Optional: Google Calendar (OAuth per user, tokens server-side) to create the event and invite the advisor.

**Test:**
- Many parser unit tests (`src/test/parse-followup-time.test.ts`). Freeze "now" with `vi.setSystemTime`, and cover IST midnight edge cases and English/Hinglish phrasing.
- Simulate a `consultation_booked` webhook and check the meeting appears with the right time and owner.
- Running the same webhook twice must not create two meetings (idempotent by call id).

**Done when:** a consultation booked on a call shows up as a meeting with the right time and owner within a minute of the call ending.

## #17: End-to-end tests for the call to lead flow

**Assignee:** Charan Varigonda · **Branch:** `feature/17-e2e-tests` · **Depends on:** #18 seed data (start with your own fixtures if #18 isn't merged yet)

**Why:** catch regressions in the most important flow automatically.

**Build:**
1. Add Playwright: `npm i -D @playwright/test`, `npx playwright install chromium`. Config in `playwright.config.ts` with `webServer` starting `npm run dev`. Tests go in `e2e/`.
2. Seeded test workspace and user (from #18). **Mock Sarvam**: the outbound call request is intercepted or stubbed, and the test then POSTs a simulated payload to `/api/public/sarvam-call-webhook`.
3. Flow per case: sign in → place a test call → send the webhook → check the call shows Completed, the lead appears under Leads → Interested, the deal is in the right pipeline stage and the follow-up task exists.
4. Cases: interested; consultation booked (stock agent); not interested (no new lead); do-not-contact (contact blocked and the next call refused); webhook missing (the sync path).
5. CI: add a job to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that runs `npx playwright test` on every PR, uploading the HTML report as an artifact when it fails. Test credentials come from GitHub Actions secrets, never from the repo.

**Test:** break a mapping on purpose (for example interested → wrong stage in `crm-outcome.ts`) and confirm the suite fails, then revert.

**Done when:** the suite runs green in CI and fails if a disposition mapping is broken.

## #20: Website lead-capture widget with instant AI callback

**Assignee:** Charan Varigonda · **Branch:** `feature/20-lead-widget` · **Depends on:** #13 helper (`isBlocked`). Uses its own widget key, **not** the #5 API key

**Why:** any website can embed a form that drops enquiries straight into the CRM, with an optional AI call within a minute.

**Build:**
1. `public/widget.js`: `<script src="https://…/widget.js" data-key="wk_…"></script>` renders a small form (name, phone, interest, consent checkbox required for the callback). Keep it dependency-free and style-isolated (Shadow DOM).
2. Migration `widget_settings` (`organization_id`, `widget_key`, `allowed_domains text[]`, `project_id`, `agent_id`, `instant_callback bool`, `colour`).
3. Public endpoint `src/routes/api/public/widget-submit.ts`: validates the widget key and `Origin` against the allowed domains, applies rate limits (per IP and per key) and spam protection (a honeypot field, plus rejecting submissions faster than ~3 s after render), and validates the phone with `normalizePhoneNumber`. Add CORS headers for allowed origins only.
4. Create or update the contact in the chosen project. If instant callback is on, consent is ticked and the number isn't blocked, place a call with the chosen agent.
5. Settings page: widget key (regenerate), allowed domains, agent, project, colour, a live preview, and copy-paste embed code.

**Test:**
- Unit tests: honeypot filled → rejected; too fast → rejected; bad phone → 400; disallowed origin → 403.
- Make a plain `test.html` page that embeds the widget (serve it with `npx serve` on another port and add that origin to the allowed domains), submit it, and check the contact appears. With callback on, your phone rings.

**Done when:** submitting the widget on a test page creates the contact, and with callback enabled, the phone rings within a minute.

## #8: UI/UX polish pass

**Assignee:** Charan Varigonda · **Branch:** `feature/8-ui-polish` (or split: `feature/8-ui-polish-tables`, `feature/8-ui-polish-empty-states`, …) · **Depends on:** nothing, but **do it last**, because it touches many files others are editing

**Why:** the app should feel consistent and easy to use on every screen.

**Build:**
1. **Audit first.** Walk every sidebar page at desktop width and at 375 px. Post a checklist comment on issue #8 (page → problems). Fix from that list.
2. Empty states with a clear next action on every list page. Loading skeletons instead of blank areas. Friendly error messages (`friendlyError` in `auth.tsx`).
3. Tables: horizontal scroll on mobile, sticky header, readable column widths, row hover.
4. Accessibility: visible focus rings, labels on every input and icon-only button (`aria-label`), AA colour contrast, keyboard navigation and focus trap in dialogs.
5. Consistency: `PageHeader` on every page, one primary button per page, toasts only for things the user can't otherwise see.
6. Bring the auth page's visual language (cards, spacing, gradients) to the landing page and onboarding.

**How to keep it mergeable:** open several small PRs (one per area), rebase on `dev` daily, and don't reformat whole files. Only change what you are fixing.

**Test:** before/after screenshots per page in each PR. Chrome DevTools → device toolbar at 375 px. Keyboard only (Tab / Shift+Tab / Enter / Esc) through sign in → place a test call → open the call → see the lead. Lighthouse accessibility score before and after.

**Done when:** every page has before/after screenshots, there are no layout breaks at 375 px, and keyboard-only navigation works through the main flows.
